segments.text: This film was typed, not drawn. NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory wrote every frame as code, and our engine rendered and measured each one.
Type a story in any language and get a short film: characters who act, voices, and an original score. There is no image generator anywhere.

This is the real run behind it, replayed from its stored trace. Nemotron 3 Ultra, the Director, plans the coverage: wide shots, close-ups, a mood for every shot, and a cast and set bible in strict JSON.

Nemotron 3 Super designs the cast as engine kits, so poses and lip sync are exact, then writes every shot as SVG. The engine renders each frame and measures it, and a failed check goes back to the artist as a measured fix.
Then a vision model describes what it actually sees, and Nemotron Nano scores the shot against the plan. A revision replaces a frame only when it scores higher.
When a shot still misses, only that shot is redone, on the same plan and cast. This film took one take and three single-shot redos: under thirty cents of model calls, its cast preview included.

The same crew made a Vietnamese New Year film about bánh chưng, and a Japanese story for Hidamari, a storytelling channel, narrated with the channel's own voice track. Every published film passed the same measured checks, then a check by eye.

Under the hood: one OpenAI compatible endpoint on Token Factory, strict JSON schemas, and each Nemotron tier sized to its job. Ultra plans, Super does the heavy drawing, and Nano makes the fast, cheap calls. Every model output passes the same validators a person's would.

We measured it honestly. On ten fixed prompts, judged blind by the same independent model as version one, the full crew scored 6.2 out of 10, up from 5.5, and beat Nemotron Super alone on seven of nine prompts. A second, stricter judge scores lower, and we publish both. Every published film then passed a check by eye.
